newsitem.title: INDIA: Foreign buying pushes Delhi shares to higher close.
newsitem.headline: Foreign buying pushes Delhi shares to higher close.

text.p: Share prices closed higher on the Delhi Stock Exchange (DSE) as foreign institutional investors and speculators stepped up buying at prevailing low level prices, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index closed 5.03 points higher at 722.24.
"Foreign institutional investors and speculators bought heavily to take advantage of the prevailing price level," said a trader.
"Share prices picked up on reports that the former prime minister got exemption to appear before the high court in person," said Suresh Aggarwal of brokers Jai Mata Securities.
Former Indian prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao won temporary reprieve in a criminal conspiracy case after police warned that militants could attack the political leader in Delhi's crowded courts.

Rao had been summoned to appear before a lower court judge on Monday to face charges and possible arrest in the $100,000 conspiracy case. He would have been the first former prime minister to appear in court in a criminal case.

The high court ruled that Rao did not have to appear in court until it meets on October 7 to decide on the police demand that the venue of the lower court hearing be shifted to a more secure location.
Reliance Industries quoted 5.15 rupees higher at 192.10 on buying by speculators and foreign institutional investors, brokers said.
TELCO rose 6.90 rupees to 454.90 and TISCO traded 2.80 rupees higher at 172.65.
DCM Daewoo closed 2.25 rupees higher at 19.50 while ITC hotels rose 3.90 rupees to 114.90.
